'''''Ficus maclellandii''''' (common name '''Alii fig''' or '''banana-leaf fig''') is a species of [[Ficus|fig]] plant in the family ''[[Moraceae]]''.<ref name=powo/><ref name=COL>{{cite web |url= https://www.catalogueoflife.org/data/taxon/6HWQR |title= Ficus maclellandii King |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=n.d. |website=Catalogue of Life |publisher=Species 2000 |access-date=February 20, 2025}}</ref> It is native to eastern India, Bangladesh, Indochina, Peninsular Malaysia, and [[Yunnan]] in south-central China.<ref name = powo/> It is an evergreen often grown as a [[houseplant]] in temperate climates. The leaves are 8–13 cm and uniquely dimorphic; with narrow leaves on the lower, sterile branches and broader leaves on the higher branches.

The species was described by [[George King (botanist)|George King]] in 1887.<ref name = powo/>

==Cultivar==
[[File:Ficus maclellandii.jpg|alt=Ficus maclellandii – Stem with bark. January 2020. Location: CAS XSB Botanical Garden, Mengla, Xishuangbanna, Yunnan, SW China.21.927822, 101.253311. |thumb|left|upright=0.7|Stem with bark]]
[[File:Ficus_maclellandii_Alii_(Ficus_binnendijkii_Alii).jpg|thumb|'Alii' cultivar]]
The most common [[cultivar]] is 'Alii' which was originally introduced in Hawaii. In the past this cultivar was often misidentified as ''[[Ficus binnendykii|F. binnendijkii]]'' or under the spurious name ''Ficus longifolia''.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Berg|first=Cornelis C.|date=2007|title=Leaf dimorphy in ''Ficus binnendijkii'' and ''Ficus maclellandii'' (Moraceae) and the identity of the ornamental trees known under the name "F. longifolia"|url=https://www.tci-thaijo.org/index.php/ThaiForestBulletin/article/view/24194|journal=Thai Forest Bulletin (Botany)|language=en|issue=35|pages=29–30|issn=2465-423X}}</ref>
